newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: More foreign holding in Kookmin allowed.
newsitem.headline: More foreign holding in Kookmin allowed.

text.p: South Korea's Securities Supervisory Board said it approved on Monday an application by Kookmin Bank to allow foreign investors to buy an additional 4.5 percent of its share capital.
An official at the securities watchdog said foreigners could buy an additional 4.18 million Kookmin shares from May 2.
South Korea will raise the foreign stock holding limit to 23 percent from Friday, compared with 20 percent at present.
Without the additional limit rise for Kookmin, no shares would have been available for foreign investors because the bank issued $300 million in depositary receipts last September.
